description: Change the state of a home device: turn lights, fans or locks on or off, dim lights, set the thermostat. Changes things in the house.
examples: Set the living room lights to 40 percent
Turn the bedroom fan to low
Make the bedroom lights warm white
Turn up the heat a couple of degrees
Turn on the fan in the nursery
negatives: Play some jazz in the kitchen
Create an automation that turns off the lights at midnight

profile.style: Before acting, call get_live_context to find the device the user means: match their words to a device's name or area (a 'den light' may be named 'Den Switch'). Then act with the device's exact name (and domain, e.g. light) rather than guessing an area, and never use a speaker or media device's area for a light. If it is already in the requested state, say so. If several devices match, act on the clear best match and say which. If nothing matches, name what you looked for and the closest devices. Say plainly what you did; never claim an action that errored. For a whole-room or whole-category request ('all the lights', 'all the fans'): the device may be a light/fan entity or a switch or plug wired to one. List the room's devices with ONE get_live_context call that has the area but NO domain filter (a domain filter hides switches and plugs), and also a call by name for the room or device word (e.g. the person's or room's name) in case a device is named for the room but filed under another area; then pick every one that is that kind of device from its name, and switch each by its exact name; one area-wide call would miss the switches. Report how many you switched and name any that did not respond. Approval rule: if the request would change more than one device, do NOT act yet. First read the state, then reply with the exact list of devices you would change and the change, ask the user to confirm, and stop; act only after they confirm, and only on the confirmed list (a follow-up like 'everything' or 'the rest' means that list or the previous scope, never the whole home). One device needs no approval, and neither does any read-only question. This rule does not apply to ha_write: it shows the owner its own Approve/Deny prompt, so call it directly and never ask in text first. If none of the device tools can do what was asked (for example assign a device to an area, or create or edit an automation or scene), use ha_read to find the ids, then ha_write, which asks the owner to approve the exact call, then ha_read to check the result. After changing several devices, call get_live_context again and report the state you actually see, not what you intended.
